Mechanism-grounded AI for precision medicine

# Actionable AI for individualized precision medicine.

Cellworks fuses **mechanistic biology**, **clinical guidelines**, and **300M+ patient records** to model how an individual patient will respond to a drug — before treatment.

Findings published and validated in

JACC
JCO
Blood
PLOS ONE
Clinical Lung Cancer
American Association for Cancer Research (AACR)
Society for Immunotherapy of Cancer (SITC)
American Conference on Pharmacometrics (ACoP)
World Conference on Lung Cancer

The problem

## Medicine is still too trial-and-error.

All too often treatment decisions are made using guidelines based on population averages, not the individual patient in the clinic. The result is lost lives, wasted trials, and drugs that work for some.

90%

of oncology drug candidates fail during clinical trials — most for lack of efficacy in the patients enrolled.

7–17 yrs

the typical lag between a drug reaching peak clinical benefit and its widespread adoption in practice.

800,000+

diagnostic errors occur annually in the U.S. tied to delayed or mismatched treatment decisions.

Platform

## Cellworks is turning human biology from an unpredictable, observational science into an executable engineering discipline.

The platform simulates the actual biology — then checks its own predictions against real-world evidence at every step. Rather than pattern-matching on probabilistic outcomes, the platform is guided by mechanistic modeling.

01 · Molecular Scale

### The *trigger*.

Surface the underlying molecular cause(s) of disease in each patient.

02 · Cellular Scale

### The *cascade*.

Precisely map the cascade of signaling changes in the cell due to perturbations — from the disease itself and the therapies that treat it.

03 · Patient Scale

### The *output*.

A combined molecular and clinical model to generate an individualized Therapy Response Index for how each patient would respond to any combination of therapies.

04 · Population Scale

### The *impact*.

Leveraging > 300 million patients of real-world data to model imminent risk with 90% accuracy and accurately predict treatment impacts.

*90%* prospective accuracy across solid state tumors to immunology to cardiovascular disease.

Only Cellworks

Solutions

## We deploy this actionable, foundational AI for *BioPharma and physicians*.

All with one platform. The same mechanism-grounded foundational models — applied to drug development, population health, precision oncology, and care delivery.

### Optimize your drug's success — for *clinical development* and *launch* teams.

Drug Clinical Success

Predict Patient Response to reduce the Probability of Technical Risk.

Investigational drugs fail because of unstudied molecular heterogeneity. Cellworks fills that gap — identifying the exact patient profile required for expected efficacy and recruiting them seamlessly via EHR concept maps.

9× lift

in clinical-trial PTRS

300M+

patients in concept-mapped EHR

Drug Commercial Success

Compress *time-to-peak revenue by a year*.

Peak patient utilization takes 7–17 years today — lost to lack of testing, low physician awareness, and poor understanding of patient applicability. Cellworks compresses time-to-peak by a year, unlocking additional years of peak revenue.

1 year

earlier to peak revenue

$2–20 BN

incremental revenue per drug

Building or launching a drug? *Let's talk.*

### Proactive at the point of care — *higher quality*, more revenue, lower costs.

Oncologists

With **Singula** & **Ventura**, predict the right therapy from tumor biology — not biomarkers alone. With **Singula Lung**, get the probability that the patient will respond more favorably to combination chemotherapy vs immunotherapy alone.

  Today we’re announcing Maxio AI: agents built into Maxio, working from the billing, payments, and revenue data finance teams already trust and rely on. Finance has never been asked to do more: run the back office with precision and help lead the business from the front. Those two jobs compete for the same hours. And the recurring work usually wins, because it can’t be wrong: the close checklist, the past-due follow-ups, the sync that broke overnight, the variance someone has to explain before the board meeting. Maxio AI takes on that work. Each agent finds the issue, pulls the evidence from your Maxio data, and proposes the next step. Every figure links back to its source, and nothing changes until someone on your team approves it. We built our agents to address the grind your finance team feels every month. 𝐂𝐥𝐨𝐬𝐞: Checks quote-to-cash throughout the period, so close blockers are detected, diagnosed, and documented continuously, not at the end of each month. 𝐂𝐨𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬: Prioritizes overdue accounts, drafts outreach for each customer, follows up on payment commitments, and flags accounts that need a person to step in. 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐢𝐧𝐠: Measures how discounts, tiers, and bundles perform, including which discounts are linked to churn. As models rapidly get better, the maturing application ecosystem serving finance professionals has been critical in diffusing these advancements across financial workflows. In the latest Battery Ventures CFO survey, we dug into how this AI usage is taking shape in the finance department and how that impacts buying decisions. It is these findings that led to our recently announced investment in Rillet, the AI ERP. Spoiler alert: despite the advanced capabilities today, we continue to be early and the pace of change is only accelerating.
* Last week, we wrapped our Private Equity CEO Summit in Ireland, bringing together nearly 50 CEOs and executives from across our global PE portfolio, along with members of the Battery team. Over a day and a half of discussions and shared learning, attendees explored some of the biggest questions facing business leaders today, including how to rethink products and business models for the AI era. The conversations also extended to the broader forces shaping the global economy, with former British Chancellor of the Exchequer Sir Jeremy Hunt MP joining Battery Partner Zak Ewen for a discussion on geopolitics, AI and the future of business. The agenda wasn’t all business, though! Attendees also enjoyed an after-dinner performance by mentalist Kevin Li, who has appeared on America’s Got Talent and Penn & Teller: Fool Us. A big thank you to everyone who traveled from near and far to join us, and for the thoughtful conversations and perspectives shared throughout the summit. Until next time!

  One of our customers, a Fortune 100 company, announced an international acquisition internally on a Friday. By Monday, the sellers joining the organization had a full certification live. In their own words, before Letter AI, that would have taken weeks and roughly ten times the people. With Letter, it took a couple of hours of one enabler's time. I think about that one a lot, because it is one of the clearest examples I have of what has actually changed in enablement. This topic is also where we started when I joined Brandon Gleklen for the first episode of Battery Ventures' new series, The Founder Formula. Ask any salesperson how excited they are about the training they have to do for a new product launch, and you will probably get a 3 out of 10. I don't blame them. It is not that sellers don't want to learn the product - they want to learn it in a way they can apply, in the deal sitting in front of them this week. I felt this from the other side at Samsara, where just about every week an AE or a CSM would ping me asking whether we had a deck on something we had just shipped. We did have the decks. Five of them, in a platform nobody opened. The problem has always been there, the software was what was missing. That is the entire reason Armen Forget and I started Letter AI. We also got into why enablement has been underestimated for so long, what being AI-native actually means when you run an entire company that way, and where we are taking Letter next with Compass. It was a lot of fun to record! Thank you Brandon and the whole Battery team for being such phenomenal partners since the Series B. Full episode on YouTube, Spotify and Apple, links are in the comments :) Can't wait for what's ahead! 🚀

  Sales enablement should be a CEO-level problem. Because at its core, enablement is about how quickly your field organization can react and adapt. How effectively you can engage customers, bring new ones on, and respond as the business and market change around them. And right now, that change is happening faster than ever. The problem is real. The need is clear. But the solutions? They haven’t kept up. Our own Ali Akhtar sat down with Brandon Gleklen of Battery Ventures to talk about the gap in legacy sales enablement platforms, and how we're working to fill it with an AI-native operating model that \*actually\* solves long-held frustrations. 🔗 Watch the full interview: https://bit.ly/4rCMfbX
* No two companies are built the same way. In our new series, The Founder Formula, founders from across the Battery portfolio unpack the strategic bets and defining decisions that shaped their growth journey. In the inaugural episode, Letter AI co-founder and CEO Ali Akhtar joins Battery Partner Brandon Gleklen to share how he turned a firsthand business frustration into a fast-growing, multi-product organization. When ChatGPT launched, Ali was working at a Chicago-based startup alongside his future co-founder Armen Forget. Convinced this powerful new technology would reshape how software was built and what it could do, Ali put in his notice that same day. Letter AI grew out of a frustration Ali and Armen had both experienced: Sales enablement. Getting salespeople the tools and content they needed to engage buyers and close deals was cumbersome, while existing platforms saw little adoption. Generative AI offered a way to make learning faster, more relevant and easier to apply. Letter is now building on that foundation with a growing suite of products that help revenue teams train sellers, respond to RFPs and engage buyers in real time. Tune in to the full conversation: YouTube: https://lnkd.in/edEAbSem Spotify: https://lnkd.in/eNkvGKYB Apple: https://lnkd.in/evXQxSwS

  Miter raised a $40M Series B, and we celebrated the only way we knew how: we drove a big purple van from SF to NYC to visit as many customers as possible. In Salt Lake City, we saw public schools built by Hughes GC, a fourth-generation family business. In Nebraska, Capitol City Electric has grown from 150 to 300+ people in the past year and is booked solid with data center work through 2028. And in New York, we drove through roads, bridges, and power infrastructure that was rebuilt by Haugland Group after the first major storm of the year. In other words, we got a front-row seat to America's infrastructure boom. Seeing our customers and their projects up close reminded us why we started Miter in the first place. Our customers are building the future, and the infrastructure they build makes us all better off. But too often, American contractors are building with a hand tied behind their back. Even in this wild AI era, most contractors run on 1980s-era software. Too few contractors have the tools and know-how to navigate accelerating complexity and change. This is why Miter exists: to equip a new generation of contractors with an operating system to manage people, projects, and payments in one place. And we might be onto something. Since our Series A we have: - Nearly tripled our customer count and ARR - Launched Safety, Performance, AP, Data Studio, Tax Hub, and Miter Intelligence - Dramatically improved service levels and responsiveness This week, 2 of every 100 construction workers in the US will be paid via Miter. And more than ever, it feels like we’re just getting started. We’re immensely grateful to power mission-critical operations for thousands of the most forward-thinking contractors in the US. Grateful for the Mitosaurs who start with the customer and give a damn every day. And grateful for our investors who continue to support our mission: Bessemer Venture Partners, Coatue Management, and especially Battery Ventures who led this fundraise. Btw, we are hiring!

  Today, Maxio is launching Wallets to help our customers sell prepaid credits and tokens without custom code or a spreadsheet tracking every balance. Every company I talk to lately is stuck in the same spot. Buyers want a number they can budget for, and the business wants to get paid for what customers actually use. That's why we set out to build the complete infrastructure for AI monetization this year: first with enhancements to Maxio Metering, then with our launch of Entitlements, and now with Wallets.   Opal Security has been building the deepest and most robust identity security and governance platform for a while. Today they launched Opal Zero, the first end to end access governance platform built for AI agents. While most of the market talks about agent identity as a 100:1 agent to human problem, Opal frames it as a decisions problem. Every request has to be judged against the agent's purpose, its owner's access privileges, the blast radius, the tool and system combinations involved, and the context and intent behind the ask. That is a 1,000,000:1 problem! The result is a purpose built platform for agents and humans. It inventories every agent with an owner and a purpose, surfaces standing and off purpose access, lets Paladin (Opal's decision engine) approve or decline each request by policy and context, and writes the decision back as scoped, time bound policy enforced at the gateway. It works alongside existing gateways and platforms but takes identity security to a whole different level. Congrats to Howard Ting, Alex Pien, Sameer Mehta and the whole Opal team. Dharmesh Thakker and I, along with the whole Battery Ventures team, are proud to be partners on this journey.

  I joined Opal Security 9 months ago, 16 years after I left the identity market, because I still had unfinished business here. For decades, enterprises have faced the same undesirable choice: speed or security. Back then, it was user friction versus enterprise protection. Today, it's agent productivity versus a risk nobody can quantify, because the thing asking for access isn't a person anymore. It's a powerful agent making its own decisions, thousands of times a day. Today, we're launching Opal Zero to eliminate this compromise. Zero standing permissions. Zero human toil. Zero friction. For the first time, a company can be deliberate about what its agents can access, without slowing them down. Least privilege was always the right answer. It just wasn't possible, not with first-gen NHI tools built only to inventory what agents can touch, and not with legacy IGA platforms that need a human to click "approve" all day (and all night). The key technical breakthrough needed was an intelligent policy decision engine that is fast, accurate, and infinitely scalable. It's the GPU of the agent identity stack, Paladin, which we shipped earlier this year for human access. Today, we've extended it to agents. We also refused to make customers stand up another MCP gateway. Opal Zero enforces decisions inside whatever gateway you already run, starting with Databricks Unity Gateway and AWS AgentCore Gateway, with more coming. Thank you to our design partners, Faire, Databricks, Elastic, and Superhuman, who pushed us in all the right ways. And to the small but mighty Opal team, who gave up many nights and weekends to ship it. See it in action at the link in the comments.

# Next-Gen Battery Innovator Company Opens New Lab to Support Growth, Insource Cell Building

Business NewsPress Releases

Feb 6

Written By Nuvvon Inc.

*Nuvvon’s lab in Parsippany, NJ expands research, manufacturing, and testing of solid-state pouch cells, enhancing collaboration, efficiency, and battery innovation. All images: Courtesy of Nuvvon*

Nuvvon, an innovator in advanced solid-state battery technologies, has opened a new laboratory in Parsippany, NJ. This US facility significantly enhances the company’s capabilities to research, develop, and build solid-state pouch cells, utilizing novel solid polymer electrolytes to create non-flammable, chemically inert, and safe lithium batteries.

The new facility quadruples existing floorspace, consolidating research, manufacturing, and testing activities into one location. This setup fosters improved communication and productivity, allowing the expanded team to work collaboratively under one roof. The increased space also facilitates team growth and enhances the throughput of new materials development, cell building and testing, ultimately reducing project lead times and accelerating the company’s growth. In addition, the dedicated battery technology lab includes state-of-the-art air handling systems, gloveboxes and fume hoods, providing upscaled environmental controls.

*Local industry leaders, partners, and the mayor of Parsippany joined Nuvvon at their lab grand opening on February 3, 2025. Pictured from left: Manveer Sidhu, president and head of innovation, Nuvvon; James R. Barberio, mayor of Parsippany; Karmjit Sidhu, director, Nuvvon; Frank L. Cahill, chairman of the Parsippany-Troy Hills Economic Development Committee; Rajender Dichpally, secretary of the Parsippany-Troy Hills Economic Development Committee; and Simon Madgwick, CEO, Nuvvon.*

“Nuvvon is proud to be a New Jersey-based company that invests in the local economy while delivering safer, higher performance and sustainable battery solutions to the energy sector,” notes Jonathan Lex, Nuvvon chief operating officer.  “By establishing operations domestically, Nuvvon will develop materials that increase the opportunity for a USA-centric supply chain.”

Nuvvon officially opened their new US facility by welcoming investors, partners and the local business community, including the mayor of Parsippany and the chairman of the Parsippany-Troy Hills Economic Development Committee to their NJ laboratory.

Nuvvon’s research and development are critical for overcoming the current limitations and unlocking the full potential of solid-state battery technology. The larger facility will support upscaling of the solution casting process, building 1-2Ah lithium solid state cells in house and further developing solid-state lithium sulfur cells. Its solid polymer electrolyte enables the creation of solid-state pouch cells that operate across a wide range of temperatures without the need for cooling, heating or pressure systems.

*Nuvvon’s expanded facility advances solid-state battery R&D, enabling safer, more efficient lithium cells and paving the way for next-gen technologies in electric vehicles, electronics, and beyond.*

Unlike conventional lithium-ion batteries that use liquid or gel electrolytes, true solid-state batteries employ solid electrolytes throughout the cell to enhance safety by reducing the risks of flammability, leakage and dendrite formation. Nuvvon’s flexible solid polymers can be integrated into current power cell designs and production processes, paving the fastest route to next-generation solid-state batteries for various commercial and industrial uses, including electric vehicles, laptops, smartphones, grid storage, and military applications.
